data.content:
## Root cause (confirmed by code reading)

`lease_expiry_ts` is a plain DB column (`knot_hot.lease_expiry_ts`,
`ALTER TABLE ... DEFAULT 0`, src/db/migrations.rs:211) that is mutated
ONLY through `db::update_lease_expiry_ts` (raw `UPDATE knot_hot SET
lease_expiry_ts=?` — src/db/catalog.rs:341), called from
`App::set_lease_expiry` (src/app/knot_lease.rs). Every caller of
`set_lease_expiry` — lease creation (src/lease.rs:38), claim/poll heartbeat
(src/poll_claim.rs:253), explicit extend
(src/write_dispatch/execute/mod.rs:424,
src/write_dispatch/execute/execute_write_ops.rs:93), and lease-guard
auto-renew (src/lease_guard.rs:185) — updates the column directly and never
writes ANY event (full or index). Separately, `UpsertKnotHot`
(src/db.rs:180) and `MetadataProjection` (src/sync/apply_helpers.rs:29),
the two structs that DO flow through events (local writes and sync-apply
respectively), have no `lease_expiry_ts` field at all, so even if an event
carried it nothing on the write path would persist it. Net effect: expiry
never leaves the machine that set it, so a pulled lease always shows the
`knot_hot` schema default of 0, and `effective_lease_state` (0 = expired)
reads it as expired.

## Design

1. **Event carrier**: use the existing `idx.knot_head` index event (a
   materialized-snapshot stream, not full audit history) rather than a new
   `FullEventKind`. Add `lease_expiry_ts: i64` to `KnotHeadData` /
   `build_knot_head_data` (src/app/helpers.rs) — always present in the
   JSON payload as a `Value::from(i64)`, sourced from the record already
   in scope (`current.lease_expiry_ts`) at every one of the 8 existing
   `build_knot_head_data` call sites (knot_scope.rs, gate_metadata.rs,
   query.rs, state_ops.rs, knot_update.rs, edges.rs, knot_profile.rs,
   execution_plan_edit.rs) plus `knot_create.rs` (0 for brand-new knots,
   since a lease's real expiry is only known after `set_lease_expiry`
   runs).
2. **Threading into the cache**: add `lease_expiry_ts: i64` to
   `UpsertKnotHot` (db.rs) and the INSERT/ON CONFLICT UPDATE SQL, and to
   `MetadataProjection` (apply_helpers.rs, `from_existing` +
   `upsert`). Every *local* writer of `UpsertKnotHot` passes through its
   own already-cached `current.lease_expiry_ts` (no behavior change for
   local writes — this is a pure plumbing addition, same pattern as
   `lease_id`/`deferred_from_state`).
3. **Absent-field = unknown, not 0-as-expired** (the acceptance
   criterion for old-binary events): in `build_index_upsert`
   (apply_helpers.rs), compute
   `existing.map(|r| r.lease_expiry_ts).unwrap_or(0)` first, then
   override with the event's `lease_expiry_ts` only `if
   params.data.contains_key("lease_expiry_ts")`. This is the exact
   existing fallback-then-override pattern already used for `lease_id`,
   `deferred_from_state`, `blocked_from_state`, `execution_plan`, etc. A
   pre-fix binary's `idx.knot_head` event never has the key, so applying
   it preserves whatever the local cache already had (0 for a
   never-seen knot) — identical to today's behavior.
4. **Root-cause propagation (heartbeats/renewals)**: `App::set_lease_expiry`
   is the single choke point every caller already goes through. Change it
   to also emit a fresh `idx.knot_head` event for the lease knot (reusing
   `build_knot_head_data` with the lease's already-cached invariants/
   gate_data/execution_plan_data/scope_data, current title/state/profile,
   and the *new* expiry), so every heartbeat, explicit extend, and
   post-create expiry assignment gets pushed on the next `kno push`. The
   payload's `updated_at` field is kept as the record's existing
   `updated_at` (not "now") so heartbeats do not bump the knot's visible
   `updated_at` / reorder `kno ls` — only `lease_expiry_ts` changes.
   `set_lease_expiry` gains repo+cache `FileLock` acquisition (it had
   none before) since it now performs a file write, matching every other
   mutator in this module.
5. **Owner guard untouched**: `recover_expired_bound_lease`
   (src/app/state_fail_ops.rs) keeps its unconditional
   `lease.lease_data.is_owned_by(&self.machine_id())` check regardless of
   `effective_lease_state`. Only the stale explanatory comment (which says
   "a live foreign lease arrives here with expiry 0" — no longer always
   true) gets corrected; the guard logic and its regression test
   (src/write_dispatch/tests_lease_ext5.rs::materialize_expired_lease_leaves_another_machines_lease_alone,
   which forces `set_lease_expiry(1)` then reassigns ownership) are
   unchanged and must keep passing untouched.
6. **Clock skew**: `lease_expiry_ts` is an absolute Unix timestamp; no
   inter-machine clock normalization is performed anywhere else in the
   codebase, so none is added here — the receiving machine compares a
   foreign expiry against its own `now_unix()` exactly as it already does
   for local leases. Skewed clocks can only make the *display* of a
   foreign lease's remaining time optimistic or pessimistic; they cannot
   cause a destructive action, because `recover_expired_bound_lease`'s
   owner guard (step 5) refuses to touch any lease this machine does not
   own regardless of what the (possibly skew-distorted) effective state
   says. Document this explicitly in docs/leases.md, replacing the
   "lease_expiry_ts is not replicated" paragraph.

## File-by-file touch list

- src/db.rs — `UpsertKnotHot.lease_expiry_ts: i64`, SQL column+placeholder+
  SET clause.
- src/sync/apply_helpers.rs — `MetadataProjection.lease_expiry_ts`,
  `from_existing`, `upsert`, `build_index_upsert` fallback/override.
- src/app/helpers.rs — `KnotHeadData.lease_expiry_ts`,
  `build_knot_head_data` payload insert.
- src/app/{knot_scope,gate_metadata,query,state_ops,knot_update,edges,
  knot_profile,execution_plan_edit,knot_create}.rs — thread
  `lease_expiry_ts` through each `KnotHeadData{}` / `UpsertKnotHot{}`
  literal (existing value; 0 for brand-new knots in knot_create.rs).
- src/app/knot_lease.rs — `set_lease_expiry` emits a fresh
  `idx.knot_head` event; adds `FileLock` acquisition.
- src/app/state_fail_ops.rs — comment fix only, no logic change.
- src/snapshots.rs — thread `lease_expiry_ts` through its
  `UpsertKnotHot{}` literals (bootstrap/snapshot load path).
- docs/leases.md — rewrite the "lease_expiry_ts is not replicated"
  paragraph to describe replication + the clock-skew/safety note.
- Tests: extend src/sync/apply_tests_event_paths.rs (or a focused new
  `apply_tests_lease_expiry.rs`) for (a) a full round trip — a head event
  with a future `lease_expiry_ts` applies and reads back non-expired, (b)
  an event missing the field preserves the existing cached value / stays
  legacy-0-expired for a brand-new knot; src/write_dispatch/tests_lease_ext5.rs
  already covers the owner-guard regression and must keep passing
  unmodified. All existing `UpsertKnotHot{}`/`KnotHeadData{}` literals in
  test files (db/tests_ext.rs, sync/apply_tests_event_paths.rs,
  replication/tests.rs, replication/tests_push_unblocked.rs,
  doctor_tests_ext.rs) need the new field added to compile.

## Test strategy (maps to verification_steps)

1. Round-trip test in sync/apply layer: build an `idx.knot_head` event
   JSON with `lease_expiry_ts` = now+N, apply it via
   `IncrementalApplier`, assert `db::get_knot_hot(...).lease_expiry_ts ==
   now+N` and `effective_lease_state` reports non-expired.
2. Same apply path with the key omitted from the JSON payload: assert the
   cached value is unchanged (new knot -> stays 0/expired, matching
   today).
3. Re-run (unmodified) `materialize_expired_lease_leaves_another_machines_lease_alone`.
4. `make sanity`.

No child knots needed; this is a single, cohesive plumbing change confined
to the sync/lease subsystem.
